name: ActivityWatch
description: New aw-tauri UI ships a wired auto-install updater whose client config has an empty verification pubkey — payload verification defeated. (Legacy aw-qt is N.)
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: The updater pubkey is an empty string in committed configuration, so no pinned verification key is present.
limitations: Source-at-commit evidence only; released artifacts and external framework enforcement remain unverified.

original_evidence.text: | ActivityWatch (aw-tauri component) | https://github.com/ActivityWatch/activitywatch (submodule https://github.com/activitywatch/aw-tauri) | activitywatch@ce5838296004605c9b8edcecad128e64e2718e31 (2026-08-22); aw-tauri@f70bcdf913db3e1648b99ba459538469f744cd26 | Y | Y (default) | Y | https (GitHub Releases + tauri-plugin-updater over reqwest/TLS; no disabled-validation code found) | Y (attempted — release CI signs artifacts w/ minisign key when `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` secret set, `includeUpdaterJson`/`createUpdaterArtifacts` toggled accordingly) | signature (Ed25519/minisign via tauri-plugin-updater) — **but the verifying pubkey shipped in the client config is an empty string** | **none pinned** — `plugins.updater.pubkey` is `""` in the committed/shipped `tauri.conf.json`; no CI step patches in a real pubkey (only `createUpdaterArtifacts` flag is patched) | `aw-tauri/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:25` (`"pubkey": ""`); `aw-tauri/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:864` (`tauri_plugin_updater::Builder::new().build()`); `lib.rs:1095-1096` (`handle.updater()` → `.check().await`); `lib.rs:691` (`download_and_install`); `lib.rs:378-383,449` (`auto_download` defaults `true`); `.github/workflows/release.yml:86-111` and `build.yml:90-107` (signing key wired into CI, pubkey never patched) |
